children: OPEC+, the alliance of oil-producing nations comprising OPEC and allies including Russia, agreed in principle to keep December oil output targets unchanged ahead of a Sunday meeting, as Gulf producers pump below quotas amid Iran war disruptions.
The decision was reported by Reuters on Saturday, citing three people with knowledge of the matter.

According to the report, seven core members met online: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman. The outcome matches expectations that no further output policy changes will come until next year.

The decision lands as U.S. fuel prices remain elevated. According to American Automobile Association data, regular gasoline averages $4.1837 a gallon, 16.6% below its June 2022 record, while diesel at $6.3101 sits just 3.3% below its all-time high of $6.5276, set on Sept. 22.
Brent crude, the global benchmark, rose above $113 a barrel on Friday, up nearly 11% in a month and about 75% in a year, and within 3% of its four-year high of $116.72.
